details.description: Fixed service structure only: truss column, walkway grating, floodlight heads. No vehicle surface in this zone.

Tank ogive nose and the start of the barrel. Two details read clearly: the nose-to-barrel transition ring, and a vertical conduit ridge running down the barrel offset from the centreline, casting its own thin shadow. The white vent-hood arm above the nose belongs to the tower and is excluded.
Night sky. No vehicle, no structure, no usable evidence.
Tower mid-section, orbiter access arm and service platforms. The white vertical strip at the left edge is tower plumbing, not the vehicle.

Densest zone. Orbiter black nose cap with a hard boundary against white; a bright window group on the crew module in two bands; a dark band sweeping aft-and-outward from the forward fuselage on both sides, symmetric about the centreline; a small dark circular port below it. Both booster nose cones are visible as a steep cap over a shallower frustum with a step between. The tank behind shows the waisted intertank band with a brighter structured surface than the barrels.

Starboard booster case as a clean straight cylinder with a constant diameter over this span, terminated by its nose cone at the top. Confirms the booster barrel is untapered and gives the cleanest diameter measurement in the frame.
Tower base, platform deck edge and pipework. No vehicle surface.

Wing planform with a visible sweep break between a shallow inboard glove and a steeper outboard panel. USA and a flag sit on the wing upper surface. The trailing edge carries a dark band split into inboard and outboard segments. A narrow bright vertical blade at the centreline is the fin seen nearly edge-on. Below it a dark aft bay contains the clustered engine nozzles and the body flap.

Starboard booster lower case and aft skirt. The skirt flares to a visibly larger diameter than the case barrel. A dark rectangular patch sits on the case surface partway up. The starboard wing tip crosses in front of the booster, confirming the wing extends beyond the booster outer envelope.

detailInventory.note: Nine grid zones filled from the 3x3 contact sheet. Four zones carry no vehicle surface and are recorded as excluded rather than invented. The component-level inventory with fifteen entries lives in _shuttle/assessment.json and is the one the spec consumes; this grid pass is the spatial cross-check that nothing on the vehicle was missed.

authoringInstruction: Filled from direct inspection of each zone crop.
